stem.text: Let \( y = f(x) \) be a twice-differentiable function. Suppose that \( \left. \frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} \right|_{x=2} = 1 \). Write this statement in prime notation, and state what it means.

answer_key.label: \( f''(2) = 1 \), so the rate of change, with respect to x, of the rate of change of y when x = 2 is 1.

worked_solution.text: In \( \left. \frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} \right|_{x=2} \) the function is f, the independent variable is x, and the second derivative is evaluated at x = 2, so the statement is about one input only.
In prime notation the same statement is \( f''(2) = 1 \).
It says that the rate of change, with respect to x, of the rate of change of y when x = 2 is 1.

options.label: \( \left(f'(2)\right)^{2} = 1 \), so the square of the rate of change of y with respect to x when x = 2 is 1.
options.derivation: the second derivative written as the square of the first derivative

options.label: \( f''(x) = 1 \), so the rate of change, with respect to x, of the rate of change of y, the same at every x, is 1.
options.derivation: the point of evaluation dropped, so a value at one input is read as the second derivative function
